differences.what: Lower surrounding wall slopes outward while doorway stays recessed behind vertical cutback sides.
Header now has shallow sloped shoulders and raised center rather than a rectangular top.
One broad threshold sits inside the entrance; both former projecting treads are removed.
Foliate field is physically recessed behind a hollow archivolt and stepped mouldings.

T-2912, arch proportion: the sheet draws the head STILTED, not a semicircle on the spring line. Read at 100 px a foot, the extrados is 6.48 ft across and stands 7.06 ft over the spring (centre 0.58 ft up), the tympanum's ring 2.51 ft across and 2.93 ft high (centre 0.47 ft up), and both run plumb down to the spring; the office's doorway No. 23A draws the same. Built: centre 0.5 ft over the spring, extrados 6.5 ft, springers and the tympanum's fillets, billet channel, archivolt floor and rolls carried plumb to the spring. Residual: the fan's crown sits within 0.06 ft of the sheet's, the tympanum ring's about 0.1 ft high.

T-2912, the fan's joints: fifteen voussoirs keyed at the crown, radiating from the stilted centre, the two springers' outer and inner faces plumb to the spring line as the sheet draws its lowest stones.

T-2912, the carving at the drawing's grain: the sheet draws eight stems bent into rings in the field, unequal and not mirrored, four low and four high, rising from a boss at the foot; the build had five on a mirrored trunk. Built: the sheet's eight at its places and sizes (docs/RESEARCH/glessner-entry-T-2853/), on stems from the foot boss. The leaves inside each ring are below the sheet's stipple and stay the owner's photographs' rosettes (reconstructed carving, LIBERTIES).

T-2912, door leaf and hardware: the sheet draws the leaf of 1963 (a seven-by-seven grille with spear tips and no figures, no strap, a knob at the left stile, one lower panel). The period photograph a18-gh-glessner-front-with-keith shows the figures 1800 a fifth of the way down the leaf and a knob at mid-height on its centre line, where the office's sheet No. 95 puts the grille's number row and the strap's boss, and neither is on the 1963 leaf; so the sheet records a later leaf, not the 1904 one, and the build keeps sheet No. 95 (L-glessner-front-door-2216). This picture cannot show the 1904 leaf.
Ivy beside the door: the 1963 drawing draws no planting; the vine is the period photographs' (T-2225) and is not carried forward or back from this sheet.

T-2949 (of T-2913) read the courses beside the door; T-2955 owns building them. At the sheet's own scale (the door's outer frame 494 by 751 px on the 400-dpi scan, 98.8 px a foot; this crop is rectified on sheet 6's 7.75 ft door and runs about 3 % tall), the Prairie elevation draws sheet 5's printed string (18, 18, 15.5, 9.5, 13.5, 14.5, 7.5 in) up from its base line 0.54 ft under the sill: its first seven beds at 0.92, 2.40, 3.70, 4.56, 5.70, 6.94 and 7.58 ft against the string's 0.96 ... 7.50 from that line, and the 1888 photograph a18-gh-glessner-front-with-keith shows the same joints. The ticket's 6.1 was not a bed. The build lays the same string from the walk 0.74 ft under the sill (beds 0.76, 2.26, 3.55, 4.34, 5.47, 6.68, 7.30), 0.20 ft low everywhere. It is not raised here: one coursing serves every granite face, and on 18th Street the apertures are set on the string's sums from north grade (L305), so raising the beds alone pulls them off those windows, and raising the Prairie face alone breaks the NE corner's returns. Read as level courses round the corner, the sheet measures the 18th Street grade 0.20 ft over the Prairie walk, the offset grade_datum takes as zero; T-2955 sets it and carries both. Above the head the sheet's drawn courses run long against the printed inches, as its 18th Street elevation does against the string printed beside it; the printed inches govern there (docs/RESEARCH/glessner-entry-T-2853/T-2913.md). T-2955 set it: grade_datum's north grade 0.20 ft over the walk and the granite string laid from it, its bottom course run down to the walk. On the re-solved camera (T-2971) the render's beds beside the door fall at 1.00, 2.49, 3.79, 4.58, 5.70, 6.91 and 7.53 ft over the sill, against the string's 0.96 ... 7.50 and the drawing's own lines at 0.94, 2.41, 5.66 and 7.53 read in the same strip: every bed within 0.05 ft, the base line at -0.55 against the drawing's -0.51.

T-2949 (of T-2913), the header stone: the sheet draws it one course high from the door head to the spring, its end joints 5.09 ft left and 5.08 ft right of the door's centre line, a stone about 10.17 ft long (S 27.8-38.0); nothing falls at S 36.0. Built: S 27.8-38.0, from 27.9-37.9.

T-2950, the door's height against the seventh bed: sheet 6 gives the door 7.75 ft and the build keeps it, so the head stands 0.25 ft over the seventh bed joint (7.50); sheet 5 draws the door 7.60 ft at its own scale and puts the head on that joint, and the 1888 photograph's door (about 1.49 times as high as wide) agrees. Settling it moves the leaf, the header and this view's camera, which is solved on 7.75 ft. T-2971 (of T-2950) built it 7.50 ft, the head on the seventh bed: no sheet prints the height; sheet 6 read at its own printed 0.00 and 24.30 draws the frame 5.05 by 7.60 ft, sheet 5 7.60, the photograph about 7.4, and both sheets put the head on the bed the printed string sets at 7.50. The header's foot follows the head to 7.50. The camera is re-solved on the scan's own pixels, 100 px a foot both ways, no longer stretched 3.3 % to force 7.75 (habs5-entry-T-2950.png).

T-2972, found by T-2971: on the re-solved camera the sheet draws the header one course high, from the door head (7.50) to bed 8 at about 8.75 ft, its top flat, with the fan springing from bed 8; the build springs the fan at 9.0 and raises the header's centre to 9.3, so the header stands about 0.25 ft too tall at its ends and 0.55 at its centre. T-2912's spring, stilt (0.5) and crown were read on the old crop, 3.3 % tall, so all read high (spring about 8.78, stilt about 0.35 unstretched); the raised centre is the owner's close-up's (T-2228) and has to be argued against the flat-topped drawing. T-2972 read it on the square crop at 100 px a foot and built it: the header's top lies flat at 8.73-8.79 ft either side of the tympanum and rises in a shallow segment under it to about 8.89 at the centre; the extrados's outer line fits a radius of 6.49 ft about a centre at 9.16 (its inner line 6.41 at 9.12, the tympanum's ring 2.50 at 9.13), the crown at 15.65, the plumb legs down to the header's top. Built: the header one course, door head to bed 8 (8.71 by the printed string), its top flat to the shoulders with a 0.14 ft segment over the tympanum's 5 ft (the owner's close-up's raised centre at the drawing's height and width; the office's 23A simplifies that edge and the built HABS detail controls it); the fan springing from bed 8, stilted 0.43 ft (centre 9.14) to a crown at 15.64. On the re-render the header's top, the raised segment, the extrados, the crown, the voussoir joints and the tympanum's ring lie on the sheet's lines in an overlay of the two.
